stories.headline: Ukraine hits Russian warship off Libya
stories.summary: Ukraine says sea drones sank the Russian corvette Merkury at Benghazi, Libya, in an early-morning strike on Sunday. Ukraine's security service said seven drones were launched from a mothership, and Zelenskyy praised the operation as exemplary. The Kremlin warned of an "escalation of tensions in the region" but declined to comment directly on the Libya attacks.

stories.headline: Russia warns Estonia and Ukraine
stories.summary: Russia has threatened 'hostile' Estonia with 'open war', accusing Tallinn of hostile actions including a border closure and of letting Ukraine launch attacks. Moscow also warned Ukraine of a 'dangerous trend' after the Libya and Baltic attacks on its shipping. The items do not say how Estonia responded.

stories.headline: Ukraine war reaches NATO territory
stories.summary: NPR reports the war is spilling into NATO territory, with attacks on ships, missiles in Poland and fresh allegations of Russian operations inside Denmark. Denmark has previously accused Russia of plotting an assassination. Germany also warned that Russia could place a nuclear weapon in space within 60 days, citing intelligence it is 'taking seriously'.

stories.headline: COP31 climate talks collapse with no deal
stories.summary: The longest UN climate summit in history ended in Antalya, Turkey, without a final deal, the first such failure in 17 years. Oil-producing countries' interests, a US boycott and a dispute over finance were cited as reasons. Australia, which co-hosted, blamed 'difficult geopolitical times', and carbon capture and removal emerged as a key divide.

stories.headline: Israeli strikes continue in Gaza
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed at least three people in Gaza, including UNRWA employee Adel al-Helou, who was killed on duty on Monday. Gaza continues to see attacks despite an October 2025 ceasefire deal. Oxfam says Israeli attacks have turned Gaza into a 'toxic wasteland', with signs of possible contamination across almost all of the territory.

stories.headline: Fire at Indonesian confectionery factory
stories.summary: At least 24 people have been confirmed dead in a fire at a confectionery factory in Indonesia. About 30 people are still missing, and rescuers are searching unstable structures, with DNA needed to identify victims. Separately, a boat tragedy in Nigeria has prompted a search for survivors, with the government blaming overcrowding, poor maintenance and missing life jackets.

stories.headline: Manchester arena evacuated after unknown substance
stories.summary: More than 12,000 people were evacuated from Manchester's Co-op Live arena after an 'unknown substance' was released during a Don Toliver concert. Police are investigating, and concertgoers described a horrible smell and screaming, with one person taken to hospital. Don Toliver has postponed his O2 arena show in London as a result.

stories.headline: Nvidia's Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO
stories.summary: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive after a surprise return, and its shares rose about 33%, adding around $1tn in value. The Nasdaq was up about 7% and US stocks had their best day since April 2025. Trump said he 'made the deal' and said the administration had assured Nvidia's board Huang would not be a national security threat, while lawmakers vowed to press for public testimony.

stories.headline: Capita shares plunge after boss quits
stories.summary: Capita shares fell about 70% after chief executive Adolfo Hernandez left with immediate effect. He admitted the company 'has not delivered' for retired civil servants waiting for pension payments, which are overseen by Capita. The scheme's problems have continued since last year.

stories.headline: Compass plans US listing switch
stories.summary: Compass, the £43bn NHS caterer and one of the largest FTSE 100 companies, plans to move its primary listing from London to New York. The decision would be another loss for the London market, following a growing number of firms leaving the UK to list in the US.

stories.headline: Poundland faces collapse
stories.summary: Poundland has days to find a buyer or face administration. The item asks what has gone wrong but the summary available is limited to that deadline.

stories.headline: Energy bills and European gas prices rise
stories.summary: European gas prices surged as a forecast cold snap raised fears of a supply shortage this winter, following slower Qatar supplies and depleted summer stocks. Household energy bills are also about to increase in the UK.

stories.headline: Brazil's real hits 19-month low
stories.summary: Brazil's real fell to a 19-month low as a post-election selloff deepened after President Lula's re-election. Investors have doubts about his commitment to reining in swelling government debt.

stories.headline: Anthropic IPO and AI market worries
stories.summary: Anthropic raised $81bn in the largest initial public offering on record, with its co-founders now very wealthy. Analysts and investors are increasingly worried about an AI bubble, and Citadel Securities warned that markets are signalling a darkening growth outlook.

stories.headline: Trump open to capping credit-card rates
stories.summary: President Trump said he is open to capping credit-card interest rates, though MarketWatch advises holiday shoppers not to count on it yet. Separately, the Labor Department proposed a rule that could curb ESG funds in 401(k) plans.

stories.headline: Liverpool thrash Man Utd 4-0
stories.summary: Liverpool beat Manchester United 4-0 at Anfield, with Rio Ngumoha starring. Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes, leaving United with ten men. Mauricio Pochettino's first game as United head coach left them in the relegation zone.

stories.headline: Hull beat Brighton with stoppage-time double
stories.summary: Oli McBurnie scored a stoppage-time double as Hull City beat second-placed Brighton 2-1 in the Premier League. Goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis, who had conceded seven for Greece nine days earlier, played a pivotal role. The item does not give the full score.

stories.headline: England and Australia cricket
stories.summary: Australia's Chaudhary won the first T20 against England, and a last-over finish at the MCG suggested a series of fine margins. England have lost Will Jacks to a series-ending injury. Former South Africa batter AB de Villiers said he has 'no doubt' Australia tampered with the ball in the first Test of the 2018 series.

stories.headline: Rugby: England, Ireland and Wales
stories.summary: England beat New Zealand by a record margin, and England wing Tommy Freeman is in contention for the Nations Championship play-off rematch on Saturday. Ireland beat South Africa, with Andy Farrell saying it 'sets us up nicely' for next year's World Cup. Wales face Japan in their autumn finale after the Wallabies narrowly beat them in Cardiff.

stories.headline: Thitikul wins LPGA Tour Championship
stories.summary: World number two Jeeno Thitikul shot a seven-under 65 in the final round to win the CME Group Tour Championship for a third successive year.

stories.headline: Carbon removal divide at COP31
stories.summary: Carbon capture and removal, along with climate finance, emerged as fault lines at COP31, which ended without a deal. Carbon Herald also reported that Storegga has exited the Acorn CCS project as EnEarth acquires a 30% stake. The East Coast Cluster has awarded more than £2.25bn in UK supply chain contracts.

stories.headline: Nigeria biochar and Rwanda agroforestry carbon deals
stories.summary: Investment in carbon removal continued, with VP Capital investing in Nigeria-based biochar carbon removal by AirSmat. Removall Carbon also partnered with Green Solutions & Supply on an agroforestry project in Rwanda.

stories.headline: GTA 6 hacker released on licence
stories.summary: Arion Kurtaj, now 21, pleaded guilty to the Rockstar Games hack and others he carried out as a teenager. He was released on licence with a warning 'don't let this happen again'.

stories.headline: Iranian singer flogged for performing without hijab
stories.summary: Lawyers say Iranian authorities flogged singer Parastoo Ahmadi, three musicians and a producer, with 74 lashes each reportedly given in Qom. The item does not give any official response.

stories.headline: Russell Brand's wife on prison message row
stories.summary: Russell Brand's wife said she will honour prison rules after a row over a message from her inmate husband. She said she will stick to the 'parameters' after reading out his message.

stories.headline: Jilly Cooper accused of plagiarism
stories.summary: Analysis reportedly finds striking similarities in dialogue and narrative structure between Jilly Cooper's novel Prudence and works by two contemporaries. The bestselling author, who is late, has been accused of 'extensive and deliberate plagiarism'. The items do not report a response.

stories.headline: Music and entertainment news
stories.summary: Molly Meldrum, the Australian promoter and broadcaster who helped define Australian music tastes for decades, died aged 83. Miley Cyrus married Maxx Morando in a California ceremony. Steven Spielberg is reportedly making a western scripted by Paul Thomas Anderson.

stories.headline: Walrus habitat protected in Alaska
stories.summary: American conservationists have secured permanent protection for barrier islands off Alaska's Bering Sea coast. The area is home to the largest concentrations of Pacific walrus in North America, around 200,000 walrus, near the village of Point Lay.

stories.headline: Volunteer finds lost toddler in desert
stories.summary: Arizona volunteer Jay Stewart found a missing toddler in the cold desert at night. He was honoured by the sheriff's office as an outstanding citizen.

stories.headline: Baxdrostat reverses hormone-driven high blood pressure
stories.summary: A study of an FDA-approved drug, baxdrostat, showed it reversed high blood pressure caused by hormones, with effects lasting years after treatment. Doctors described the results as extraordinary.

stories.headline: India pledges $1.6bn to Nepal
stories.summary: India pledged $1.6bn to Nepal to help it rebuild after deadly floods, as Nepal's prime minister Balendra Shah visited New Delhi. The funding comes alongside port access and a new train service.

stories.headline: Blade Runner 2099 and Focker In-Law reviews
stories.summary: Guardian critics describe the new Blade Runner 2099 series as baffling, and the fourth Focker film, starring Ariana Grande, as overfamiliar. The contrast reflects how sequels and revivals continue to dominate screens.
